body: Alternative Investments: The Types, Benefits, & Risks You Need To Know. You’ve successfully built a solid investment portfolio with traditional assets like stocks and bonds, but lately you’ve been hearing more about alternative investments. There’s often greater risk in these alternative markets, especially for investors who are unfamiliar with their specific mechanisms. The factors you look at to make good investment decisions are usually pretty different from the ones you’d consider with more traditional investments. Understanding alternative investments and the part they play in diversifying your portfolio can help expand your options. Traditional assets form the foundation of a strong portfolio, while alternative investments can broaden your financial horizons. * Include crypto, private equity, real estate, hedge funds, commodities, and more. These investments typically require more specialized knowledge and often come with different rules and structures than traditional investments. If you are considering alternative investing, it’s important to work with a specialist who can help make the most of your portfolio.

An investment portfolio can paint a clear picture of a person and their goals for the future. Traditional investors might limit their selections to asset classes such as stocks, bonds, and cash. However, for those savvy investors looking to both embrace innovation and fill gaps in their portfolios, there are other options. Alternative investments are any disparate asset that is not the traditional publicly-traded option of a bond, stock, cash, etc. However, some alternative investments are still considered a common vehicle to pursue, such as real estate or commodities. Some typical alternative investments are hedge funds, cryptocurrency, private equity, venture capital, derivative contracts, managed futures, and tangible assets such as antiques and art. There may also be different lengths of time when the money is locked in before an investor can access it. When diving into alternative investments, you want to be sure to establish an alternative strategy suited to your needs and desired level of risk.

# The Pros and Cons of Alternative Investments. Investing in Alternative Assets: Pros and Cons. Alternative investments have been getting increased attention, but they typically involve higher risk, limited liquidity, and more complex fee structures. * Things to consider before investing in alternative investments. ## What are alternative investments? ## Pros and Cons of Alternative Assets. With some alternative investments, you may lose access to your money for years. Even if the alternative investment is packaged in a mutual fund wrapper, the fund may not have daily liquidity. A common selling point of alternatives such as venture capital and private equity is the ability to get in on the ground floor of the next great company. The right half of the chart shows returns for venture capital, private equity and hedge funds (all considered a form of alternative investment). It’s important to fully understand all fees associated with an alternative investment and how they will impact the investment's performance before committing to buy.
